# NOTES: Thomas Wingfold, Curate (George MacDonald), Vols I–II (text as given)

Source: Project Gutenberg #5973 (Vol I) and #5974 (Vol II). Three-volume novel; text here = Vol I (Ch I–XXVIII) and Vol II (Ch I–XXXIV). Vol I ends "END OF THE FIRST VOLUME"; Vol II ends "END OF THE SECOND VOLUME." Note: the system/context block at the end of the prompt is not part of the novel; it is unrelated.

## BOOK 1 (Vol I) — chapter by chapter

**Ch I Helen Lingard.** Nov. wind; Helen (23, tall, blue-eyed, dark-haired, fair-skinned, "over still" expression, never called Nelly; drawing-master: she'd "wake up about forty") at window, then fireside, bored after a novel whose heroine married an unworthy man. Brother Leopold at Cambridge (she wrote him a letter). Helen's father: officer in India, married Hindoo lady; mother died at Helen's birth; Helen raised by widowed aunt Mrs. Ramshorn. Father left fortune split between Helen and Leopold (Leopold ~3 yrs younger). Helen dozes off; maid brings "kitchen-tea." George Bascombe due to dine.

**Ch II Thomas Wingfold.** Curate, 26, walks Osterfield park, sits by river (Lythe) on stone; Glaston abbey church. Horace's ode "quam memento"; he translates into English verse. Has never doubted/questioned church; honest in a dull way; "never thought about being a gentleman, but always behaved like one."

**Ch III The Diners.** Mrs. Ramshorn: widow of late Dean of Halystone; wants Helen's fortune kept in family; nephew George Bascombe (son of her younger sister, married to a northern canon) is meant for Helen. Wingfold invited as foil; curate of Abbey; non-resident rector, presentation belongs to rector's family. Wingfold described: ~30-looking, middle height, good forehead, questionable nose, grey eyes, black hair, pale. Bascombe: tall, handsome, "Apollo," "shirt-front," says "Don't you think?" less than Wingfold. Helen plays piano woodenly.

**Ch IV Their Talk.** Dinner talk: poetry (a volume of verse Helen got; Bascombe despises "wailing" poets); Heine parody; Horace (Bascombe likes his common sense; Wingfold likes his sad submission). Bascombe sings his own song "Each man has his lampful" (Sun and Wind; "the day draws nigh when we all go out"). Helen: "heathenish."

**Ch V A Staggering Question.** Moonlit street outside Mrs. Ramshorn's (red brick, Queen Anne style). Bascombe with cigar: "do you believe one word of all that!" (pointing at church tower). Bascombe: Christians fear death; Horace more honest. Wingfold silent; Bascombe: "I honour you" for silence; "Good night."

**Ch VI The Curate in the Churchyard.** Wingfold sits on gravestone at night, doubts; considers Paley, Butler, Leighton, Neander, Coleridge, Liddon. Sunday coming; feels hypocrisy.

**Ch VII The Cousins.** Bascombe described: "prophet" of new order; iconoclast; Cambridge; London editorial offices; wants to convert Helen; not in love but admires; wants to marry-ish. Helen's education described (thorough bass, Euclid, drawing), no inner awakening. Garden of Mrs. Ramshorn's house (old manor-house, gardener's stupidity). Bascombe walks into garden; Helen joins.

**Ch VIII The Garden.** Helen declines cigar ("I like it diluted"). Bascombe on "creation," born-fools, "Wingfold"; argues against punishment-by-heaven/hell, for "mutual compassion" and "the good of the whole"; Helen impressed. Bascombe considers marrying Helen (cosmos is "prolific darkness of non-intent").

**Ch IX The Park.** Walk in park; birds in winter; old house (Glaston house) in hollow near lake; legend of lady drowned in sack. Helen and Leopold ("Poldie") used to explore; a hidden trap-room in house closet ("well big enough to hold three"). Leopold feared that room.

**Ch X The Dwarfs.** Meet Joseph Polwarth (huge head, asthmatic, pigeon-breast) and niece Rachel (under 4 ft, crooked, high shoulder). Bascombe: such people should not marry; proposes laws; Helen says "unfortunately they have all got mothers." Church service: Litany, Communion, sermon on forgiveness. Bascombe leaves; Helen loves Leopold, described as Hindoo-eyed, "a love of a boy."

**Ch XI The Curate at Home.** Wingfold's inner crisis: doubts whether God exists; prays; tries uncle's sermons (uncle Dr. Jonah Driftwood, D.D.; 157 sermons left him); finds all doctrinal ones unsuitable. Resolves to preach the odd sermon.

**Ch XII An Incident.** Wingfold finds a small manuscript volume dropped by Rachel on path; returns it to Rachel and Polwarth; "I have not read one word of it." Wingfold's inner anguish continues; Sunday passes in a fog. Hawthorn bud makes him weep; child smiles at him.

**Ch XIII A Report of Progress.** Bascombe courts Helen (making love); Helen receptive but not in love. Bascombe's arguments ("truth is truth"). Neither proposes formally.

**Ch XIV Jeremy Taylor.** Letter from Joseph Polwarth (The Park-Gate): Wingfold's sermon was Jeremy Taylor's, unacknowledged. Wingfold reflects on sermon-borrowing.

**Ch XV The Park Gate.** Wingfold goes to Park-Gate lodge; Rachel answers door; Polwarth's cottage (thick thatch). Rachel's hair, face, small hands. Polwarth: asthmatic, white hair, dry husky voice.

**Ch XVI The Attic.** Polwarth's attic study, books everywhere. Polwarth says preaching others' sermons honestly OK, but must be above-board; urges Wingfold to preach own heart. Rachel brings tea.

**Ch XVII Polwarth's Plan.** Polwarth: "bread from another baker's shop." Wingfold confesses: can't prove God; asks if Jesus existed. Polwarth: "I know him in my heart." Polwarth: "as well ask a fly... if it is round."

**Ch XVIII Joseph Polwarth.** Polwarth's life: Cornish ancestors who lost Osterfield; father tall and handsome; brother Robert (engineer, died at 50, left Rachel £20/yr); Polwarth has £30/yr; schoolboy bullying; secret attic "nest"; boy he chased into pond; conversion via reading Matthew 1:21 ("he shall save his people from their sins"). Asks: "How do I know there is a God?" / "How am I to know such a man as Jesus ever lived?" Polwarth: "I have seen him."

**Ch XIX The Conclusion of the Whole Matter.** Polwarth: "take your New Testament... read to find out." Wingfold will keep curacy for a month while searching; resign if no light. Wingfold: "You are the first real friend I have ever had—except my brother, who is dead."

**Ch XX A Strange Sermon.** Wingfold's sermon on "Confessing your faults one to another": he confesses reading uncle's sermons as his own; reads extracts from old divines (gleaned fields). Mrs. Ramshorn indignant; Bascombe changed view ("plucky"), wants to help him. Helen says she's glad he thinks so. Mrs. Ramshorn suspects rector hands sermons; reveals her late husband (dean) relied on her writing sermons.

**Ch XXI A Thunderbolt.** Night, ~1 a.m.: Leopold taps at Helen's window (roof balcony). He confesses murder; "they are after me." Helen takes him in; brandy; he is wild; blood on wristband. He says he killed a woman (Emmeline) with a skean-dhu knife.

**Ch XXII Leopold.** Leopold (20, swarthy, dark eyes, slight) begs "save me." Helen swears "so help me God, I will not" give him up. He says "They must have found her"; "old shaft"; wants to hide. Helen takes him through garden to the old house.

**Ch XXIII The Refuge.** They go to old house (hidden room over trap). Leopold recalls his dread of it; Helen sings him to sleep. Leopold has a small silver box of drug; a knife he keeps; asks Helen to whistle when returning.

**Ch XXIV Helen with a Secret.** Dawn; Helen flees home; faints. Day: she keeps composure; visits Polwarth lodge-gate area, walks to shops. Dissimulation begins.

**Ch XXV A Daylight Visit.** Helen returns to old house in daytime; prays briefly ("I am his sister, thou knowest"). Passes Rachel singing at lodge.

**Ch XXVI Leopold's Story.** Background: Leopold (~16) knew the manufacturer's family (Yorkshire, near uncle's Goldswyre). Met Emmeline (eldest, flaxen, vain, cold); she toyed with him; he took the drug. Emmeline engaged to Captain Hodges.

**Ch XXVII Leopold's Story Concluded.** Masked ball; Leopold in cloak, mask, drug-induced vision; note "Meet me for one long minute at the circle"; Emmeline: "I am going to be married to Captain Hodges"; he stabbed her with skean-dhu (silver-mounted, name engraved). Fled; sat on pit-shaft edge; fled to Helen.

**Ch XXVIII Sisterhood.** Helen: "I would rather be you than she." Helen takes the knife, puts it away. Helen's love for Leopold; the knife with his name engraved.

**Ch XXIX The Sick-Chamber.** Night: Leopold screams; Helen moves him to her room. Aunt Mrs. Ramshorn is told; Mr. Faber (new doctor, cold, practical) attends; brain-fever. Helen nurses; gets weaker; resists George.

**Ch XXX The Curate's Progress.** Wingfold reads New Testament with Polwarth; question about miracles; Polwarth: "Was Jesus true?" Polwarth prays for him.

**Ch XXXI The Curate Makes a Discovery.** Wingfold realizes he has never obeyed Jesus ("Why call ye me Lord..."). Next Sunday he preaches honest confession; congregation scandalized; Helen sees him; Mrs. Ramshorn calls him Socinian/infidel. Polwarth "dare to love him."

**Ch XXXII Hopes.** Leopold recovering; Helen believes he's innocent (hope from the illness dreams). Helen goes riding with Bascombe Saturday evening; Leopold: "If you forget me, an enemy will think of me."

**Ch XXXIII The Ride.** Ride at sunset across park to deserted house. Bascombe on death ("no consciousness of ceasing"). Bascombe tells of murder case: coast-guardsman saw boat with third man; police suspect "some squire of low degree"; Bascombe "strongly inclined to take the matter in hand." Helen: "We must get him out of the country." END VOL I.

## BOOK 2 (Vol II) — chapter by chapter

**Ch I Rachel and Her Uncle.** Rachel envies Helen's strength/riding. Polwarth on contentment vs grumbling; Rachel's temper (apologizes, kneels). Wingfold comes, asks Rachel's uncle for verses.

**Ch II A Dream.** Polwarth's poem (Lord, hear my discontent: "I am the door..."). Wingfold: "I am simply stupid" with verse. Polwarth's dream: Sinai manuscript, Armenian convent, Apostle John burns the book: "the Word of God... abideth... in the heart of the man that in love obeyeth him." Wingfold: "I trust I have the lesson too."

**Ch III Another Sermon.** Wingfold's second sermon: "Lord, Lord"—Love your enemies, Be perfect, lay not up treasures, Take no thought, Judge not, Do unto others, "Not every one that saith unto me Lord, Lord..." Mrs. Ramshorn: "takes too much pains to prove himself a pagan." Bascombe: "says what he means."

**Ch IV Nursing.** Helen nurses Leopold; Mr. Faber suspects softening of brain; Helen's health failing; reads Arabian Nights to Leopold. Leopold in sleep: "Oh Helen, darling, give me my knife. Why will you not let me die?"

**Ch V Glaston and the Curate.** Town gossip about Wingfold (fanatic, Romanizer, hypochondriac). Bascombe mocks Wingfold's faith. Poem: "O Lord, if on the wind..." Wingfold's prayers.

**Ch VI The Linen-Draper.** Mr. Drew (linen-draper; pug-nosed, rosy, kindly, deacon at a chapel; wife left him ~20 years earlier with another man). Drew troubled by business ethics; resolves to change practices (percentages to sellers, pressing debtors). Wingfold: pray. Drew: "How would Jesus have done as a draper?"

**Ch VII Rachel.** Wingfold visits Rachel (white room, "dwarfie"); her happiness; dreams of freedom; "If there be a God..." Polwarth: "Ye are the temples of the Holy Ghost." Rachel: "Some of us a little ruinous!"

**Ch VIII The Butterfly.** Wingfold's walk and thoughts; sonnet "Methought I floated sightless..."

**Ch IX The Common-Place.** Drew at closed shop: sells soldiers' wives cloth at cost; account of wife; hymn "Let me stand ever at the door." Drew will give up deaconship but keep pew/subscription.

**Ch X Home Again.** Wingfold meets Bascombe: thanks him for opening eyes; "Not yet" resigning. Sonnet "Methought that in a solemn church I stood."

**Ch XI The Sheath.** Polwarth tells Wingfold of night in park, cries, the old house, the woman in ball-dress running in, the youth's voice, and gives Wingfold the leather knife-sheath. Helen's face comes to Wingfold's mind.

**Ch XII Invitation.** Wingfold reflects on suffering, guilt, Christ's invitation: "Come unto me all ye that labour."

**Ch XIII A Sermon to Helen.** Wingfold preaches on Matthew 11:28 "Come unto me... rest"; Helen weeps; Bascombe annoyed.

**Ch XIV A Sermon to Himself.** Wingfold writes "Yes, Master, when thou comest..." Helen and Bascombe argue at garden; Bascombe scorns Christianity ("old Jew fable"); Helen: "Thank you, Cousin George."

**Ch XV Criticism.** Mrs. Ramshorn and Bascombe critique sermon. Bascombe's "murder" theories; Helen's sorrow.

**Ch XVI A Vanishing Glimmer.** Helen with Leopold: "Come unto me"; Leopold: "she is DEAD—I killed her." Helen's despair; Bascombe's doctrine of death.

**Ch XVII Let Us Pray!** Helen decides to consult Wingfold; Leopold says Milton's Satan etc.; Helen sings "Come unto me" from Messiah; kneels by Leopold.

**Ch XVIII Two Letters.** Helen writes to Wingfold (asks meeting; "P.S. Pine Street at eleven"). Wingfold replies: meet at Polwarths' cottage garden.

**Ch XIX Advice in the Dark.** Helen (veiled) asks about "wrong that had been done"; Wingfold: confess to God; "Is someone neglecting something he ought to do?" Helen faints nearly.

**Ch XX Intercession.** Helen faints; Polwarth prays over her. Helen flees home. Polwarth: "Wait for what will come next."

**Ch XXI Helen Alone.** Helen's anguish in summerhouse; she despises the curate's advice; prays once more. Leopold calls her: "I saw her" (Emmeline's ghost in mirror, worm on shoulder). Leopold: "if you don't let me see Mr. Wingfold, I shall go mad."

**Ch XXII A Haunted Soul.** Leopold insists on seeing Wingfold; Helen fetches Wingfold ("Are you quite honest with me?"). Wingfold shows Helen the sheath; "There is something dark on the lining." Helen: "You have been acting the spy, sir!" She begs him not to make Leopold give himself up.

**Ch XXIII Compelled Confidence.** Wingfold sees Leopold; embraces him; Leopold tells full story ("Do you know you came in close behind HER?").

**Ch XXIV Willing Confidence.** Wingfold: confession, "Let us keep our shame." "Jesus... I will give you rest."

**Ch XXV The Curate's Counsel.** Leopold: "Did God make me sleep, Helen?" Helen's jealousy of Wingfold.

**Ch XXVI Sleep.** Helen's conversation with Wingfold; Leopold sleeps; praises Wingfold; "He's coming again tomorrow."

**Ch XXVII Divine Service.** Wingfold brings Drew to Polwarths; Polwarth on "divine service" (serving God vs. communion). Drew's shop as temple.

**Ch XXVIII A Shop in Heaven.** Rachel reads Polwarth's vision: heavenly shop with no money; man kneels in tears; no one judged for not kneeling.

**Ch XXIX Polwarth and Lingard.** Leopold dresses; Polwarth visits him; Leopold resolves to confess ("I want to give myself up"). Helen furious; Leopold collapses. Wingfold and Polwarth leave.

**Ch XXX The Strong Man.** Bascombe visits Leopold; suspects madness; plans to take Leopold to magistrate Mr. Hooker on Monday, with Wingfold. Bascombe suspects Helen's feelings for Wingfold.

**Ch XXXI George and Leopold.** Leopold asks Bascombe how hanging is; Bascombe philosophical ("what's done is done"). Bascombe reflects on Helen's danger.

**Ch XXXII Wingfold and Helen.** Helen confronts Wingfold in library; Wingfold rebukes her pride ("let your pride die for him"); Helen angry, realizes he's right.

**Ch XXXIII A Review.** Wingfold reflects on his spiritual change (golden weathercock, "Peter-cock"); poem "Father, I cry to thee for bread."

**Ch XXXIV A Sermon to Leopold.** Wingfold preaches "I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance"; repentance and resurrection; Helen and aunt in pew. END VOL II.
